summary: ```markdown # CLO Skills Mini Class - Custom Strap Pull Tab ## Introduction Hello everyone! This video is for you to explain how to make a self-designed cloth zipper. ## Opening the 3D Window First of all, we open the window of the drawer. We need to create an OBJ component of the zipper. ## Adding the Zipper Component Then, we find our zipper on the component side. Locate the zipper inside and double-click to open it. You will see that there is an OBJ file available. Find the zipper you want to use and double-click to add it to our window. ## Setting Component Type and Units Select the component type, then ensure the unit is set to millimeters (mm). In this case, the entire zipper is 10 times the original size, which is useful for packaging. After adjusting, click OK. ## Closing the Drawer Window After adding the zipper, close the drawer window. You can see that the zipper is now added in the 3D window, positioned at the coordinate point. ## Self-Defining the Zipper Position Next, we need to self-define the zipper position. The self-defining position must be aligned with the coordinate point so that it can be correctly added to the zipper. Align it first as this will make it more convenient when it falls out. ## Simulating a Plate Below the Ground You can adjust the zipper position lower than the ground. If we want to simulate a plate below the ground, we can use the simulation attribute of the 3D window. In the blank of the 3D window, open the right arrow and click on the small triangle on the ground to close this conflict. This allows us to simulate normally on the ground. ## Freezing the Component It's essential to freeze the component. If it is frozen, it will not move from its position. ## Changing Zipper Size If you want to change the size of the zipper, select the component in the object window, then select the zipper. In the attribute editor, adjust its size. For example, if you want the Y-axis to become shorter, unlock the fixed ratio and change it to a smaller value. Then, reposition it. ## Creating a Cloth Plate on the Zipper Now we create a cloth plate for the zipper. First, choose the shape tool and click in the 2D window. Set the width to a value a bit narrower than the zipper, which is 60 mm, so we create a width of 40 mm and set the height to 200 mm. Click to confirm. ## Positioning the Cloth Plate In the 3D window, move the cloth plate using the positioning ball to a position near the zipper. Use the world coordinate positioning ball to keep the position consistent regardless of the view. ## Cutting the Dragon Layer We will cut the dragon layer. Set aside the inside of the dragon layer in the 3D window and divide it into two parts. Switch to the editor sewing line tool to keep only the sewing lines of the upper and lower ends. Change the particle diameter of the sheet to 5 mm and the conflict thickness to 1 mm. Turn on the simulation to see the natural simulation of the sheet. ## Adding Sewing Lines To make the sheet flatter, add a sewing line in the desired position using the small blue dot. Create an internal multidirectional line, then sew it up. Also, add another sewing line and use the sewing line tool to sew sections together. After sewing, remember to change these two sewing lines to overlays and simulate again. ## Editing the Sheet If you need to edit the sheet, such as stretching it a little longer at the bottom by 3 mm, you can do this. After simulation, check for conflicts in the sheet. Change to the texture surface display to ensure the sheet appears correctly positioned in front of others. ## Applying Fabric Now we can apply the fabric. In the library window, find the fabric you want to use. Search for it, then drag the desired fabric to the original fabric to cover it and add texture. Simulate again to see that the fabric becomes stiffer. ## Adding Stickers Next, we can add another sticker on top. Choose a sticker and right-click to add it. Place it on our 2D window panel. If the sticker is too large, we can shrink it. ## Exporting the Pull Tab Once everything is complete, we will export this pull tab as an OBJ file. Find the file holder and name it, paying attention to the export options. Choose all the panels, stickers, and accessories, and set to save as a zip file. Ensure the correct proportions are selected. ## Saving the Project File After saving, locate the zip file you just saved and decompress it. This is the file holder where we have our final file saved. ## Conclusion If there are follow-up changes, they can also be made on the original file. Remember to adjust the ratio and ensure everything is set correctly before finalizing. That's it for our custom pull tab! ```
